blindSummary:
This state/province presents the clearest documented border-checkpoint pattern in the country of profiling gender-nonconforming appearance as a suspicion trigger for foreign infiltration. In early August 2024, police reported apprehending 15 nationals of the neighbouring country, including seven transgender people, in separate incidents within 24 hours; the group intercepted at one border check post numbered seven — per police accounts two transgender individuals plus others they described as "disguised as third-gender" persons — a framing that treats trans appearance itself as evidence of disguise for infiltration. In November 2024, coordinated 24-hour operations across the state/province detained twelve more foreign nationals, including minors and transgender people. The state/province shares an 856 km border with the neighbouring country. These are named security-force operations with published counts — a patterned enforcement practice directly facing any trans-presenting visitor crossing by land.

While the country has no statute criminalising trans presence, this state/province's checkpoint regime converts gender-nonconforming appearance into an independently sufficient reason for detention and deportation proceedings.

A transgender welfare board has been constituted here (one of only 12 such bodies nationwide), but a right-to-information investigation found most of these boards leaderless or inactive, with no compliance mechanism or real power — an institutional presence that does not offset active police profiling at the border.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional security-news report (2 Aug 2024): in 24 hours the state/province's authorities apprehended 15 nationals of the neighbouring country including seven transgender people in separate incidents; a first group was intercepted at a border check post carrying forged national-ID and tax documents; the state/province shares an 856-km porous border. Primary count for the August sweep.

Regional news report (2 Aug 2024): seven foreign nationals apprehended at a border check post on the highway from the state/province capital en route to the country's financial capital — per the article, two transgender individuals plus others police described as "disguised as third-gender" persons. Source of the explicit disguise framing.

Regional security-news report (9 Nov 2024): in coordinated 24-hour operations across the state/province, twelve foreign nationals including minors and transgender people were detained; a post-midnight group of six included three transgender persons, bound for the country's financial capital. Establishes the pattern recurring months after the August cluster.

The government's official press portal (8 Dec 2021, the ministry in charge): state-wise list of the 12 states/provinces and centrally administered territories that had constituted transgender welfare boards under the national transgender rules — this state/province included. Official record of the board's existence.

Right-to-information investigation by a national news outlet (5 Nov 2024) into state transgender welfare boards: most of the 12 constituted boards lack a compliance mechanism or real power and were found leaderless or inactive — the basis for treating board existence as nominal rather than an offset to border profiling.
blindOutOfScope: General border-security enforcement along the neighbouring country's frontier (people smuggling, document fraud) affects all travellers and residents of border districts; only the gender-appearance-as-disguise framing is trans-relevant.
blindLocalsOnly: Resident-facing: welfare-board machinery and forged-identity-document crackdowns on local residents; the checkpoint sweeps are the visitor-relevant element.
